subject: Post-demo: inference ops gap briefing + proposed SLO tests and timeline
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: inference ops gap briefing + proposed SLO tests and timeline

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next tests so we can compare behavior vs the hyperscaler environment you ran earlier.

TL;DR: Acme asked for: (1) failover simulation behavior (region and model-level fallbacks), (2) rate-limit and throttling characteristics under burst traffic, (3) error-budget burn patterns for heavy multi-tenant workloads, and (4) end-to-end latency percentiles for your golden prompt set.

What we captured from the call:
- Primary concern: predictable tail latency during concurrent patient-record retrieval + summarization flows.
- Secondary: graceful degradation when a preferred region is unavailable (you want automatic fallback but with deterministic cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Procurement wants a clear list of tests we can run and an estimated schedule for evidence to attach to your vendor evaluation binder.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a dedicated eval window):
1) Failover smoke: simulate regional outage and validate automatic model fallback (30m window, measure 99th and 99.9th pctl).
2) Burst throttle: controlled fan-out to simulate 2x, 5x, 10x normal concurrency to measure error rate and effective per-client rate limiting behavior.
3) Steady-state long-run: 4-hour ramp at representative token distribution to observe error-budget burn and KV-cache efficiency.
4) Golden-prompt latency P0: run your canonical 120 prompts at production token lengths and report p50/p90/p99 with/without KV cache priming.

Deliverables we'll supply: a short SLO comparison spreadsheet (attached), the demo recording, and a test-run methodology doc. We can also provide a short script that reproduces the fan-out tests so you can validate on the hyperscaler side.

Proposed owners and dates:
- 05/10: failover smoke (owner: Rishi)
- 05/12: burst throttle (owner: Ben)
- 05/14: long-run and golden-prompt (owner: Markus & Rishi)

Action: can you confirm a 2-hour window on 05/10 where we can coordinate with your SRE (or give us a CloudPrime test account) and confirm whether procurement needs additional paperwork before we start? Once confirmed we'll lock the schedule and share a lightweight runbook.

Attachments: [Attachment: slo-comparison-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)], [Attachment: demo-recording-20270504.mp4 (video, 45MB)], [Attachment: acme-mutual-action-plan-v2.pdf (pdf, 60KB)]

— Markus

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference ops gap briefing + proposed SLO tests and timeline

Thanks Markus — that plan maps to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SRE access: we can provide a short-lived CloudPrime test key for the 05/10 window but need to confirm with infrastructure. I should have that by EOD 05/06.
2) Procurement asks: can you include a one‑page statement of what data (if any) would transit CloudPrime during tests and whether logs contain PHI? We need that to attach to our compliance binder.
3) Failover expectations: we expect less than 1% request failures during failover windows, and any model swap should be visible in trace IDs for debugging. Can you confirm Redwood can emit the model-version header and a trace id in responses?

We'd like to add a final test: chaos-reconnects (simulate brief TCP resets from a percentage of clients) to see how well the client-side SDK (and your runtime) recovers.

If you can answer the procurement/data question and confirm headers/traces, we can greenlight the 05/10 window.

— Jordan
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Health
j.ellis@acmehealth.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference ops gap briefing + proposed SLO tests and timeline

Jordan — great, thanks for the quick response and the additional test suggestion. Short answers below so procurement and SRE can move forward: 

- Data & logs: during the tests we do not persist PHI to any long-term storage. Traces and short-lived logs (rotated and redacted per our test run policy) will be available in the test report; we'll provide a one‑page technical statement to attach to your binder (I will send by EOD 05/06).
- Response headers: yes — Redwood will emit a model-version header (x-redwood-model-version) and a trace id (x-redwood-trace) on every response in the test harness. We'll include an example curl and SDK snippet in the runbook.
- Chaos-reconnects: agreed — we'll include a 10% reconnect test in the burst-throttle matrix (brief TCP resets for a subset of clients) and track its impact on tail latency and emitted error codes.

Schedule confirmation: please treat 05/10 09:00–11:00 PT as tentatively reserved for the failover smoke; once you confirm SRE access we will send a calendar invite and the lightweight runbook. Ben and Rishi will run the fan-out and failover steps and will provide a live log stream for debugging.

Next steps from us to you (by EOD 05/06):
- One‑page data & logs statement (Markus)
- Runbook + curl/SDK snippets (Ben)
- Preliminary SLO comparison sheet with test criteria highlighted (Rishi)

If procurement has a DocuSign or access agreement to speed test keys, cc it and we will sign ASAP.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into the binder.

— Markus
